title: Regional surge availability matrix and GPU slice plan for sustained bursts
summary: Operational planning sheet that translates per-region peak token/QPS projections into recommended GPU slice allocations and explicit headroom targets for 15-minute bursts and 30-minute sustained surges. This is intended to be the working input for capacity buys, prewarm pool sizing, and SLA safety margins for hosted API clusters.
assumptions: Primary model mix weighted: 60% large gen (long-context), 30% medium LMs, 10% embeddings/rerank
Average token per request distribution derived from telemetry (median 75 tokens, p95 420 tokens)
Slice packing: default slice = 1/4 of A100-80GB (configurable), live slice packing efficiency 0.88
KV-cache hit rate assumed 12% on average; prewarm reduces cold-start tail but consumes slice capacity
Network egress and CPU not the limiting factor for these regions under target scenarios
We target 20% usable headroom for 30-minute sustained surges and 35% for 15-minute short bursts as operational policy unless noted

headroom_targets: Operational policy: maintain >=20% headroom for 30-minute sustained surges across all hosted-api regions
Short burst policy: maintain >=35% headroom for 15-minute bursts where regional latency SLOs (<100ms p95) must be preserved
Slices reserved for prewarm pools count toward headroom budget; we recommend explicit accounting line items
Headroom expressed in tokens/sec is preferred for capacity buys (token is primary billing unit)
When utilizing smaller-quantum GPUs (e.g., T4/RTX) convert slice equivalence to A100-80GB baseline via throughput coefficients
failure_mode_analysis: Model OOM or slow kernel path under long-context requests: observed at sustained p95 sequence length > 2048; mitigations: dynamic routing to quantized variants or cap sequence length
Region-level network outage: fallback policy routes 60% traffic to nearest healthy region; capacity must be available in target region (accounted in buffer targets)
KV-cache cold start causing elevated token cost for first 60s of surge: prewarm pools of slices reduce this but increase reserved capacity
Autoscaler lag: if scale-up time > 90s then short bursts will overload available slices; plan for pre-allocated burst pools sized per projection table
Hardware degradation (1–2% GPU loss): include an availability adjustment factor in procurement (we model +2% spare across fleet)
